answer: Witnesses back their attestations with a stake that is slashed if the attestation proves false, and the pearl of the design is that the stake is locked before the event and released only after verification. The marble of the scheme is that lying costs real money, so witnesses only attest what they actually saw. A Sybil cannot buy false attestations cheaply, because each lie risks the witness's stake, and the signal of the slashing is enforced automatically on proof of fraud.
